title: Answer to Question: On the Details of the Political Situation and Its Fluctuations in Central Asia
text:
Answer to Question: On the Details of the Political Situation and Its Fluctuations in Central Asia

Question:

It is noticed that the political situation in West Turkestan (Central Asia: Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan) is a fluctuating situation. At one time we find this ruler under the cloak of Russia, and after a while we find that he has moved and is striving towards America... and so on. So can the current political situation in those republics be clarified? And may Allah reward you with good.

Answer:

Before going into the details of the political situation and its fluctuations in Central Asia, these matters must be grasped:

1- When the former Soviet Union disintegrated in 1991 CE and its republics separated, Russia realised that it was necessary to keep a firm bond with these republics because they are on its flank... So it set out at first to try to gather them in what is called the “Commonwealth of Independent States”, but many of that group slipped away from it, and some of them did not enter it from the beginning, such as the three Baltic states... So after that it set out on the “Shanghai” organisation, then common security, then collective security, then rapid reaction...

Russia also made use of its pillars which it established in these republics in the era of the Soviet Union, the most prominent of which are:

a- The demographic change that the Soviet Union brought about, especially in the republics of Central Asia, as it moved Russian inhabitants to them, and these remained in those republics as a “Russian arm”...

b- The Russian bases which were spread in those republics and did not all withdraw; rather some of them remained present in the republics of Central Asia, and they are centres of influence and forward lines for Russia.

c- The nuclear and missile testing grounds where tests were conducted in those republics, especially Kazakhstan because of its vast area...

d- Some economic ties with those states, such as the gas and oil lines...

2- Although the disintegration of the Soviet Union produced a near collapse of the Communist Party and its removal from rule... in the republics of Central Asia the former heads of the Communist Party remained the rulers, i.e. those who were there in the era of the Soviet Union continued in rule. That was by a malicious plan, so that the authority in these republics would remain fighting Islam and those working for it even after the demise of the Soviet Union, out of fear that Islam would spread effectively in those republics, so that they would unite on the basis of Islam, rule by it and perform jihad in its path...

3- The disintegration of the Soviet Union was an opportunity that America did not let slip. For Central Asia, besides being on Russia's flank, is in wide contact with China, and this makes it a strategic region for America. Therefore it began spreading its agents, its apparatuses and its intelligence services, and more importantly its money, to create footholds for itself in those republics.

Thus Central Asia is a vital interest and a strategic region for Russia and America, and the conflict between them no sooner calms than it moves anew. Therefore it is not strange that the influence, and the type of agency of the rulers of that region, change from time to time according to the effective forces that each side uses:

* As for Russia, it has its previous pillars: the demographic change that it brought about previously – let us call it the Russian community in those republics – as well as its previous bases and its economic relations...

* And America with the generous carrot that it offers to those states, i.e. financial aid, as well as suggesting to them that Russia is no longer a major state that frightens them, and its promise to protect them...

* This is from the side of the hot conflict between Russia and America in the region.

* As for the other side, it is the rulers' enmity to Islam and to those working for Islam, and this is a matter on which both sides of the conflict agree.

After that we review the political reality of those republics:

1- Kyrgyzstan: We know how Bakiyev came to rule with Russia's support in 2005 CE, and then his term was renewed in the last elections held on 23/7/2009. Russia's support for him was clear, as was America's dissatisfaction with him, for the American embassy in Bishkek issued a statement in which it said: “The United States shares the concern expressed by several observers regarding the presidential election and its results. And while some aspects of the voting process appeared positive, the United States, with the initial observations of the independent observer teams, sees that a large number of the international commitments of the Kyrgyz Republic were not met in the election.” Its statement called for “strict application of the electoral laws throughout the whole electoral process in accordance with the international commitments of the Kyrgyz Republic” (AFP 2/8/2009). Meanwhile the Russians blessed Bakiyev's election, and the Russian President Dmitry Medvedev visited Kyrgyzia on 31/7/2009 and met him to bless him and to announce his support for him before his official inauguration for a new presidential term on 2/8/2009. It was announced that the Russian President's visit to Kyrgyzia came within the framework of a conference of the Collective Security Organisation in the Kyrgyz city of “Cholpon-Ata”. The “Russia Today” page mentioned on 1/8/2009 “that the Russian President Medvedev signed today, Saturday 1/8/2009, in the Kyrgyz city of Cholpon-Ata, a document on the development and subsequent improvement of the basis of the bilateral contractual legal relations that regulate the presence of Russian formations on Kyrgyz territory and the stationing of an additional Russian unit in this country. The document also provides for the establishment of a joint training centre for Russian and Kyrgyz military personnel.” This page mentioned: “that the two presidents agreed to draft and sign a special agreement on the establishment of a military base for rapid reaction forces in the south of Kyrgyzia for a period of 49 years, with the possibility of extending it for another 25 years.” It also mentioned “that Bakiyev indicated that the agreement, which must be signed before the first of November next, will define the entire Russian military presence in the country.”

As for Bakiyev's renewal of the lease contract of the American Manas air base after he had threatened to close it, this does not indicate his moving away from Russia and heading towards America. Rather, it was done with Russia's permission, by way of appeasing America so that it would not move its followers in Kyrgyzia against the whole regime, for they are capable of disturbing the “comfort” of the regime, and consequently of affecting Russia's own bases present in Kyrgyzia. To clarify that, we mention the story of the base from its beginning:

Bakiyev tried to close the American Manas air base. In February of this year, the President of Kyrgyzia Kurmanbek Bakiyev announced from Moscow that he would close the Manas base (Reuters 12/2/2009), and he clarified that further by saying: “Over the last three years I personally raised the issue of increasing the base's rent with senior American officials. I always told them we must review the terms of our agreement; prices have changed and Kyrgyzstan is in a difficult financial situation.” And he continued, saying: “And they always answered us: fine. They repeated that over years, but how long can we wait? We are a sovereign state; we must have respect for ourselves.” (Reuters 12/2/2009).

It is understood from that that the problem of the regime in Kyrgyzia is obtaining money. It is also understood from that that the Americans paid him no attention for three whole years while he was pleading with them. The Kyrgyz parliament, which is under the control of Bakiyev's party, took a decision to close that base in the faces of the Americans, and it gave the Americans a period of 180 days to leave within this decision of the Kyrgyz parliament. Before this period had passed, it was announced in the middle of last July that an agreement had been reached between the two sides. The American embassy in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzia, issued a statement on this agreement, stating in its statement: “The Government of the United States and the Kyrgyz Republic announce the success of their negotiations on the continued use of the Manas air base” (Al Jazeera 15/7/2009). It was mentioned that its rent was raised to 150 million dollars a year after it had been 17! The truth is that it had previously been “a basic rent of 17 with aid of 133, making the total 150 million dollars a year”, and according to the new agreement this has become “a basic rent of 60 with aid of 90, making the total 150 million dollars a year”. That is, nothing changed in the matter of the rent; rather the financial and non-financial aid that was given to Kyrgyzia was named as rent instead of the word aid, and that was to save the face of Kurmanbek as president of the country who wants to have respect and to show that his state has a sovereignty that is respected, as he said!! The New York Times on 24/7/2009 indicated what we said above regarding Bakiyev's actions, as it mentioned that: “the agreement recently signed by the governments of Kyrgyzia and the United States to extend the use of the American Manas air base is nothing but a means of saving the Kyrgyz government's face before its retreat from its previous decision to close the base, such that under it the annual rent of the base is raised.” Russia was behind that, as the new agreement was announced after the meeting of the President of America Obama and the President of Russia Medvedev in Russia on 6–8/7/2009, and Russia's agreement to allow American and Atlantic supplies to pass through the territory of Russia and the territory of its allies. Russia fears for its base in Kyrgyzia at “Kant”; it fears that if it does not agree to America's base there, America will set about working to stir up unrest and colour revolutions in an attempt to topple the regime of Bakiyev, which secures its interests in Kyrgyzia for it.

All of that indicates Bakiyev's loyalty to Russia, and that Bakiyev's allowing the Americans to continue using the Manas air base in their operations against the Muslims in Afghanistan is nothing but to satisfy the Americans so that they do not move to topple him as they did with his predecessor Askar Akayev. That was with the agreement of the Russians, to preserve their presence and influence in Kyrgyzia, out of fear that America would work to destabilise him and then remove him.

As for why there is this conflict between Russia and America, it is because of Kyrgyzia's important strategic location in Central Asia. It has a border with China whose length is 858 km, so if America won it, it would become stationed on China's border. Kyrgyzia is of utmost importance for America in its work against China and in the whole region. Its base at Manas is a basic centre in its war on the Muslims in Afghanistan from 2001 until today, where more than 1000 American soldiers are permanently present. The Kyrgyz government knows nothing of all that goes on in the Manas base, because the agreement stipulates that none of the Kyrgyz inspectors or observers, or anyone else, enters the base, and nothing of the American shipments that enter and leave the base is inspected. It is entirely beyond Kyrgyz oversight, and consequently beyond Russian oversight. The “Russia Today” page mentioned on 31/7/2009, while relating the news of Medvedev's visit to Kyrgyzia and the subject of the military agreements he signed with Bakiyev, that “Kyrgyzia enjoys an important and distinguished strategic location in the Central Asia region, and for many years it has been distinguished as a point of intersection of the interests of the states of the West and Russia”. That is, there is a conflict between Russia and the states of the West, headed by America, over this strategic location. The American General David Petraeus, commander of the American Central Command forces, recently made a visit to three of the states of Central Asia, among them Kyrgyzia, the other two being Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. The Russian news agency “Novosti” reported on 20/8/2009 that observers described his visit, i.e. General Petraeus's visit, as successful, “as officials in the three capitals affirmed to the United States' envoy that they want to increase cooperation with Washington”. This visit is part of the serious American activity in these countries, among them Kyrgyzia, in an attempt to win them and to strengthen the American presence in them. Although the Kyrgyz President Bakiyev did not meet the American general, the latter met the Foreign Minister of Kyrgyzia. And although Bakiyev still realises that America is not satisfied with him and has cast doubt on his election, he fears it because of the strength of its followers inside and outside, so he wants to appease it. Therefore he settled the matter of the Manas base with it and allowed it to use it without changing the conditions, except for the trickery over their wording regarding the money, which preserves his respect and the sovereignty of his country, as he says!

2- Uzbekistan: The expression “fluctuation” applies most of all to the President of Uzbekistan, “Karimov”. After the disintegration of the Soviet Union, Karimov's gradual moving away from Russia appeared clearly. Russia formed the Common Security Organisation in 1992 CE to preserve the cohesion of the republics of the former Soviet Union, or some of them, and then changed its name to the Collective Security Treaty in 2002 CE in imitation of the North Atlantic Treaty... Karimov was of fickle temperament towards these organisations. He had previously left the Collective Security Treaty and joined the organisation (GUAM), which consists of countries opposed to Russia from the bloc of the collapsed Soviet Union, such as Georgia, Ukraine and Moldavia. But he soon left it and returned to the Collective Security Treaty after America and the Western states demanded the sending of investigation teams into the Andijan massacres in May 2005, while Russia and its allies supported him and stood by his side in his brutal massacres in Andijan and elsewhere... Now that America has closed the subject of those massacres and the subject of human rights linked to American interests, and has begun contacting him and working to draw him to itself, he has returned and shown a freezing of his activity with the Russians, and has become ready to show his activity with the Americans and to work with them. That was at its strongest when Russia saw that the Collective Security Treaty did not meet its security needs and its ambitions for sovereignty and influence, so it resorted to the so-called Rapid Reaction Organisation, i.e. rapid reaction to any threat to Russian influence in the region. Uzbekistan stood in its face and did not sign the agreement on the founding of the “Rapid Reaction Forces” and their deployment in the area of the Collective Security Organisation, which includes Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzia, Tajikistan, Armenia and Uzbekistan. The leaders of these states had decided on 4/2/2009 to establish the rapid reaction forces, or by another name the rapid deployment forces. They signed this agreement in Moscow on 14/6/2009, and Uzbekistan refrained from signing it. Karimov justified this refusal by saying: “This agreement did not define the tasks set for the joint forces.” He proposed that the agreement say: “The joint forces are established only to repel external aggression, and each state's unit of the joint forces is stationed on the territory of that state” (Novosti 26/8/2009). This shows that Karimov realises that this force will be in Russia's hand, that Russian forces will deploy in the mentioned collective security states, among them Uzbekistan, and that it can intervene in any circumstance that allows Russia to intervene in the countries of the members of this organisation, because its tasks were not defined. So he asked for them to be defined as being when an external attack occurs on these states, only and nothing else, and that no forces other than the forces of the participating state be stationed on the territory of a single state. That is, he rejects the entry of Russian forces onto the territory of Uzbekistan, and their carrying out any response to any threat to Russian influence in Uzbekistan and in the region.

Thus Uzbekistan currently is the opposite of Kyrgyzia, which agreed to this agreement and indeed added to it by allowing the Russians to set up a second base on its territory. Uzbekistan did not take part in the manoeuvres currently under way since 26 August last in the area of the Collective Security Organisation, which continue until 15 October next. Uzbekistan's conduct is considered a semi-freezing of its membership in this organisation, but it has not announced that officially. Not only this, but Uzbekistan objected to the founding of a second Russian base in Kyrgyzia because it threatens its entity, as this base would be set up close to the Uzbek border in the Fergana Valley region. The Novosti agency reported on 5/8/2009 that Uzbekistan announced, as stated in a statement published on 3/8/2009 by the “Jahon” agency affiliated with the Uzbek Foreign Ministry, “that it sees no necessity or use in implementing the plan for deploying another Russian military base in addition to the Russian base at Kant in the south of Kyrgyzia, indicating that deploying a new base might lead to destabilising the region.” And this statement of the Uzbek Foreign Ministry said: “The implementation of such projects in a complex region where the borders of three of the states of Central Asia meet may give an impetus to accelerating the militarisation of the region, inflame various forms of national confrontations and stir up radical extremist forces” (Novosti 3/9/2009). All of this indicates that Karimov's regime in Uzbekistan has recently begun to move away from Russia and to draw closer to America clearly, and among the indicators of that are:

* On 18/8/2009 the head of the regime in Uzbekistan, Karimov, stated during his meeting with the American General David Petraeus in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan: “that Uzbekistan is ready to expand constructive cooperation with the United States on the basis of the principles of mutual respect and equal partnership” (Russian Novosti agency 18/8/2009). As for the American General Petraeus, he responded to that in that he “praised the efforts Uzbekistan is making to support stability in Afghanistan and security in the region” (the same source). This shows that Karimov is expressing a desire to return to allegiance to the Americans and to being tied to them. The thorn that broke the camel's back in the previous relationship between Karimov and America was his refusal of the American demand for Western investigators to enter to investigate his massacres in Andijan, so America issued sanctions against him, and he turned his back on it, heading towards Russia, his natural backer. When America put the Andijan events behind its back, he returned to striving towards America, and America recently lifted the sanctions on Karimov's regime in Uzbekistan.

* The United States of America, which saw the state of tension between Uzbekistan and Russia, did not waste the opportunity that presented itself and sought to develop its relations with Uzbekistan, and it signed an agreement with Uzbekistan to transport the loads of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) from Uzbekistan to Afghanistan [Source: the National Centre for Strategic Studies, dated 04/04/2009]. However, the relations between the Uzbek and the American administrations were not limited to that; rather the American administration issued a letter of congratulations to Uzbekistan on the occasion of the 18th anniversary of its independence, and then Karimov accepted the visit of the American ambassador in Uzbekistan, “Richard Norland”. And before that, on 18 August, Karimov accepted the visit of the commander of the Central Command forces of the United States of America, General “David Howell Petraeus”, and a cooperation agreement was signed between the two countries containing military and training programmes and vocational education.

Thus Karimov is of fickle temperament in this respect, and his current reality is moving away from Russia and drawing closer to America.

3- Tajikistan: The political situation in Tajikistan most resembles the political situation in Kyrgyzstan. Rahmonov, the President of Tajikistan, is loyal to Russia, and he remembers their favour to him in protecting his throne, but he secures America's interests for it so that it does not stir up unrest against him, for it has many helpers in Tajikistan, though until this moment they are not in a position that enables them to change the Russian influence. So America is content now with achieving its interests... at least in the foreseeable term.

Rule was concentrated for the current President Imomali Rahmonov in Tajikistan thanks to the help of the Russian forces after a civil war that lasted from 1992 until 1997. He was able to reach an agreement with the movements that were fighting against him, such as the Popular Movement and the Islamic Renaissance Party, that elections be held and that the president's term be a single term of five years, after which free elections would be held. But Rahmonov increased the length of his stay in the first term to seven years. Then he held a referendum on amending the constitution so that he would remain in rule until 2020. Unrest broke out in 2001 in the wake of that amendment, and Russia helped him against that unrest and secured his rule for him.

Also, Russia in Putin's era strengthened its relations with Rahmonov, and Russia was able to set up a second military base for itself in Tajikistan in August 2008, twenty km from the capital Dushanbe, noting that Russia has a large military base in Tajikistan whose history extends back to 1943, called Base No. 201. The Russians also have the “Okno” station in Tajikistan for monitoring satellites and ballistic missiles. Tajikistan agreed in June 2008 to transfer its ownership to Russia for 49 years. Tajikistan is very important to Russia from a strategic aspect, so it holds on to it and tries to preserve its presence in it. Therefore it openly supports Rahmonov and his regime for securing all these capabilities for it in Tajikistan. And it tries to tie Tajikistan to itself economically so as to keep its control over it continuing. Rahmonov remembers the Russians' favour to him for helping him, enabling him to rule and establishing him in it. He made his country a participant in the Collective Security Treaty that Russia runs, and he agreed to participate in the Rapid Reaction Forces under Russia's leadership. Many people in Tajikistan depend on the money transfers of their sons working in Russia, whose number reaches half a million from a country whose population is 7 million. Tajikistan is also a member of the Shanghai organisation, which Russia runs with China's help. Russia and China recently conducted war manoeuvres in Tajikistan in the name of the Shanghai organisation, on 18/4/2009.

Nevertheless, Rahmonov behaves like Bakiyev, with Russian agreement, in not provoking America; rather he achieves for it interests that keep it silent from undertaking moves against him. Therefore, just as he allowed Russian companies to carry out projects whose value reaches 2.5 billion dollars, he also allowed American and European companies, and likewise allowed the Chinese, to carry out projects and commercial business in Tajikistan. Rahmonov offered America the use of his country's airports... Likewise he recently, on 20/2/2009, allowed the passage of American supplies through his territory to Afghanistan by way of using the Tajik railways. The deputy commander of the American forces, Admiral Mark Harnitchek, who visited Tajikistan, stated this: “We intend to ship between fifty and two hundred containers weekly from Uzbekistan to Tajikistan and then to Afghanistan. Tajikistan is extremely important since it is the closest to our bases” (Al Jazeera 20/2/2009). All of that is because Rahmonov realises that America has forces in Tajikistan that can affect his rule if he does not reassure America about its interests with him, whereupon it would move its followers seriously and effectively.

It is worth mentioning that there is to some extent a popular and party orientation in Tajikistan calling for disengagement from Russia, and there are forces in the army and in the regime calling for that, and Rahmonov realises this matter. Therefore, just as he appeases America and reassures it about its interests to keep it silent, he likewise satisfies the popular orientation against Russia. So he has made public moves in which he shows a relative distance from Russia, as the commander of the Tajik border guard openly called for the withdrawal of the Russian forces from his country. They stopped the broadcasting of Russian-speaking channels in Tajikistan and made the Tajik language the official one instead of Russian. Although these measures provoked sensitivity with Russia, Rahmonov is still closer to Russia, as we showed at the beginning of speaking about Tajikistan.

Tajikistan is strategically important because of its location bordering Afghanistan; its mountains in the south-eastern part are directly connected to the mountains of Afghanistan, and the length of its border with Afghanistan is about 1206 km. Likewise its border with China reaches about 414 km, so its importance from this aspect is like the importance of Kyrgyzia in bordering China. Therefore America will not neglect it, and it is expected that it will work to win it at any opportunity that presents itself.

4- Turkmenistan: In the era of the former President “Saparmurat Niyazov” it was loyal to Russia and headed towards it in most of its policies. But the current President “Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow”, who took over rule after “Niyazov” in December 2006, has begun working to proceed in a policy more open to the West and closer to it, and especially closer to America. In November 2007 he hosted a summit that brought together American and European officials in the energy sector and the directors of the companies BP and Chevron, alongside Russian companies. He wanted to express to them that he wants to deal with everyone, and this is what appeared from the agreements he concluded with the various parties:

* In May 2007 Russia signed an agreement with Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan to build a new pipeline that allows the gas supplies from Central Asia to be kept under the control of its company “Gazprom”, so that it monopolises the export of most of the gas from Turkmenistan. Putin considered that a victory for Russia, saying: “This agreement represents a victory for Russia, which buys gas from Turkmenistan at a price lower than what is offered in the markets” (BBC 17/5/2007). The former Turkmen President Niyazov, who headed Turkmenistan for two decades, had restricted the monopoly of gas in his country to the Russians alone and denied it to others. Therefore Russia currently, in the wake of the previous agreements, buys 90% of Turkmenistan's gas, equal to about 50 billion cubic metres a year. It buys it from it at a price of 100 dollars for every 1000 cubic metres of gas and sells it to Europe at a price reaching 250 dollars, and even more than that in the winter season, reaching 345 dollars. In Niyazov's era it bought it from it at a price of 35 dollars, until it was raised to a price of 70 dollars, and then to 100. Russia was achieving enormous profits from the gas of the Muslims in Turkmenistan. And although the price has been raised from what it was at the beginning, Russia is still achieving great profits from this gas wealth.

* In contrast, Berdimuhamedow agreed in principle to build the Caspian Sea gas pipeline in a project America supports, whose aim is to reduce Europe's dependence on Russian gas supplies. It is the line whose construction the Americans and Europeans recently signed in Turkey, called the Nabucco line (Nebuchadnezzar). It extends from Turkmenistan to Azerbaijan to pour into the pipes of the Nabucco line through Turkey to Europe. Reuters on 24/4/2009 reported an American official, whom it did not name, as saying: “Turkmenistan is the other big potential supplier for the Nabucco project, which the European Union backs. But it demands that Brussels present concrete proposals regarding its implementation.”

* China has activity in this field. The Chinese President Hu Jintao visited Turkmenistan in April 2006 in the era of the former President Niyazov, whose relationship with Russia and China was strong and allied, and the Chinese President pledged at the time to buy 30 billion cubic metres of gas a year from Turkmenistan. China extended a gas pipeline from the Amu Darya river in eastern Turkmenistan until it reaches China. It was recently announced, specifically on 30/8/2009, that China will develop a gas field in Turkmenistan by one of its companies, PetroChina, at an amount of 3 billion dollars. China has begun lending Turkmenistan hundreds of millions of dollars to help it develop its industry, because of its ambitions in its enormous wealth. The volume of Turkmenistan's gas production in 2006 reached 62.2 billion cubic metres a year, and it will be raised to reach 120 billion cubic metres by 2010.

* The enticements of America and Europe to Turkmenistan – that it will itself sell gas directly to Europe at these prices via the Nabucco line, which will be ready for use in 2014, so that this profit will be for it and not for Russia – entice Turkmenistan to be drawn to America and the West. And because Turkmenistan is a small state, it cannot blackmail Europe or pressure it as Russia does; rather it will become at the mercy of America and Europe after the implementation of the Caspian gas pipeline. Besides that, the Nabucco line will bring gas from several countries, but America will have the upper hand in it when it controls the gas sources. Turkmenistan has a large gas reserve whose estimate reaches 100 trillion cubic metres, so it is the most important and largest producer in this field in that region, and indeed at the world level. It likewise has an important oil reserve whose estimate reaches 80 billion barrels. However, oil is currently not extracted from it in large quantities; its production of it does not exceed 200 thousand barrels a day. But it is planned for production to reach 2 million barrels a day in the future.

As for America, part of the oil supplies for its war equipment in Afghanistan comes from Turkmenistan, besides there being the “Trans-Afghanistan” gas pipeline extending from Turkmenistan to Afghanistan, which transports 1.1 billion cubic metres a year there. So Turkmenistan has become important for America from this aspect as well. This is apart from its aim to control all the sources of oil and gas in Turkmenistan, and indeed in the whole world, so as to control it, maintain its hegemony over it and keep it in its grip, so that it preserves its global position as the first superpower and reduces or removes the influence of the major states such as Russia or others, in addition to achieving enormous profits in the field of energy. Therefore America is acting and focusing on Turkmenistan because it is one of the huge sources of oil and gas on which Russia depends to take it from it, or so as to acquire the lion's share of it, so that it becomes in control of it, i.e. of its suppliers and its importers. It would then supply it to Europe instead of Russia, so as to keep Europe at its mercy and under its hegemony, and likewise to weaken Russia's position and its alliance with Europe. The riddle of Turkmenistan is the conflict over its gas wealth, and in the future its oil will have a main role in the conflict.

With all this, Turkmenistan still has large economic ties with Russia, which it has not yet been able to rid itself of. America is hovering around it to catch it and take it out of the circle of this Russian influence, and Russia realises that. When Turkmenistan demanded raising the gas prices, Russia met that immediately, fearing that it would head in another direction in dealing with it and resort to America and the West to help it in that against Russia. The Nabucco project, which will divert much of its gas to Europe away from Russia, is a means of taking Turkmenistan out of the circle of Russian influence. It is worth mentioning that Turkmenistan is not a member of the Collective Security Treaty nor of the Rapid Reaction Forces, and it is not a member of the Shanghai treaty. There are no Russian military bases in it. The attention given to it by Russia, by America and the West, and to some extent by China, is in the first degree from an economic aspect, because of its richness and the abundance of its wealth of gas and oil.

5- Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan is among the largest countries in area in Central Asia, as its area reaches 2.7 million km2, and its population is very small relative to its area, estimated at between 15 and 17 million people. It was important for Russia for conducting nuclear tests in it, as it conducted 500 nuclear tests in the Kazakh region of (Semipalatinsk). Its President Nursultan Nazarbayev signed on 29/8/2009 the closure of this testing ground. Kazakhstan signed the ban on nuclear tests on 24/9/2009. America worked to strengthen its relationship with it because of its strategic geographical importance and its richness in oil and gas. It has oil wealth estimated at 100 billion barrels, it currently produces more than one million barrels, and its production is expected to rise in 2015 to 2.5 million barrels a day. It has gas wealth of about 150 trillion m3. This makes the mouths of the Western colonial states, headed by America, water over these riches, and makes them work to extend their influence to this large Islamic country rich in its riches. Its tie to America has become strong, and its president granted American companies privileges to invest in the field of oil and gas and in other fields, until American companies became the main investor in its oil and gas industry. Dick Cheney, who later became Vice President, was working in the mid-nineties of the last century on the oil advisory council in Kazakhstan, and he concluded deals in favour of American companies, among them a deal in favour of the Chevron company, in whose management Condoleezza Rice worked. The American relationship with Kazakhstan was crowned by the visit of its President Nazarbayev to America in June 2006, where he met its president at the time, George Bush. The joint statement issued by them said: “The partnership between the two states in the field of energy will help American companies explore the large reserves of gas and oil in Kazakhstan and in the region surrounding the Caspian Sea” (BBC 30/6/2006). In February last it agreed to allow America to transport its equipment and supplies overland through the territory of Kazakhstan to reach the American army and the NATO forces who are fighting the Muslims in Afghanistan. The Russian Chief of Staff Nikolai Makarov revealed at the end of last year: “plans by Washington regarding the establishment of American military bases in both Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan” (Asharq Al-Awsat 18/12/2009). It has long borders with Russia, whose length reaches 6846 km, and its border with China is 1533 km long. It has the longest shores on the Caspian Sea, whose length reaches 1894 km. Therefore it was important for America strategically and economically. It has engaged in the Partnership for Peace with NATO, and it has been counted the largest ally of the United States in Central Asia.

This is in addition to its being one of the states bordering the Caspian Sea. This sea is rich in its fish wealth, especially caviar fish, of which Russia produces annually to a value of 400 million dollars. It contains a huge oil reserve of 200 billion barrels and a gas reserve of 600 trillion cubic metres, and the mouths of America and of all the Western states water over it. This closed sea is a strategic and economic basin because of its richness in oil and gas wealth.

Nevertheless, Russia has influential pillars in Kazakhstan, and the Russian spacecraft launching station is still in it. It has strong ties to Russia, as Russia settled many Russians in it, until the proportion of Russians in it became the highest proportion in the Central Asia region, reaching between 30% and 40%. So the Orthodox Russians retain influence because of their national and sectarian ties with their original homeland Russia, even though the proportion of Muslims is the highest there, exceeding 60%.

Recently Kazakhstan has shown a rapprochement with Russia, as Russia also gives it great priority. It made it, together with itself and China, among the founders of the Shanghai organisation. It is a member of the Commonwealth of Independent States, of the Collective Security Treaty that Russia leads, and of the Eurasian Economic Community that was established in 2000 CE... It signed up to participate in the Rapid Reaction Forces whose founding Russia announced. China likewise works to strengthen its relations with it, as it extended an oil pipeline from Kazakhstan along 1240 km to supply China with its increasing oil needs.

Thus Nazarbayev wants to keep his relationship with Russia and with China strong. He once expressed his policy by saying: “If we talk about projects of bypassing the East or the West, I answer that we and Turkmenistan have a pragmatic approach” (Russian Interfax 17/5/2007). That is, he determines his policy according to what reality and the immediate interest dictate to him. Therefore, despite his alliance with America that reaches the point of allegiance, despite what has recently leaked that America has plans to set up military bases in it, and then what has been done in granting the Americans the lion's share of investment in the field of oil and gas... nevertheless Nazarbayev does not want to cut off the road to strong relations with Russia, so that his regime is not threatened.

In conclusion, Russia is trying to keep its influence and strengthen it in the states of Central Asia by all ways and means, whether through concluding regional treaties – such as the Commonwealth of Independent States, which Russia established previously in the wake of the collapse of the Soviet Union, the Collective Security Treaty and the formation of the Rapid Reaction Forces – or through bilateral treaties and agreements with each one of them and setting up military bases in each one of them, so that these states do not slip from its hand and so that it strengthens its influence in them. It likewise tries to back itself with China regionally and internationally, so it set up with it what is known as the Shanghai treaty and made the states of Central Asia participants in it. Likewise the economic treaties and projects... And in that it uses its previous pillars which it established in the era of the former Soviet Union...

Likewise America uses enticing financial aid to the states of Central Asia, in addition to making these states feel the strength of its followers inside them to stir up unrest... i.e. it uses the carrot and the stick. It also works to belittle Russia in the eyes of these states and of other states in the Caucasus and in Eastern Europe, so that no one fears it, and so as to encourage those states to dare to disobey it and to break free from its grip. The American Vice President Joe Biden said after a tour of Georgia and Ukraine: “Russia is no more than a small partner of the United States following its loss of its previous strategic role.” And he said: “The weakness of the Russian economy will force Moscow to make concessions to the West, the most prominent of which is abandoning attempts at hegemony over the former Soviet states and agreeing to reduce its nuclear capabilities” (Wall Street 26/7/2009). This explains the positions of the regimes in Central Asia, as they realise the Russian weakness towards the Americans, so they try to appease the Americans, and indeed try to head towards America.

As a result of this moving, not still, conflict in Central Asia, the political reality can be described briefly as follows:

In Kyrgyzia and Tajikistan the greater current loyalty is to Russia, while reassuring America about its interests and not provoking it by standing in its face, in order to preserve the stability of the political situation in the two countries, which could be disturbed if America moved its followers in the two countries with an effective and serious force.

In Uzbekistan it currently leans in America's favour, taking into account Karimov's fickle temperament.

As for Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan, they are an arena of “sporting” political and economic competition for America and Russia, and to some extent for China from the economic aspect.
